Hi Alice — great questions.  Pushed a few short answers here and a concrete next step.

Files / formats:
- Preferred upload: Google Drive folder (see link) or S3 presigned if you prefer.
- Manifest: CSV with columns [id, payload_type, payload_text, labels(optional)]. We included a template (prompt_evals_template.csv).

Redaction guidance:
- For workshop ingestion we ask that you remove direct identifiers (email, SSNs, phone numbers). Our redaction_guidelines.pdf explains recommended regexes and examples. For anything we miss during ingest we offer one-pass scrubbing during the session but please do the heavy lifting on your side.

Load test and test keys:
- We can run a light 5 RPS sustained window during the session using a limited-capacity test pool. We'll generate temporary API keys scoped to that run; no certs necessary. We'll also capture latency/cost metrics and share the per-route dashboard after the test.

Scheduling:
- 9/14 10:00-12:00 PDT works for our engineers. If that is OK on your side, we'll lock it and send the calendar invite with a Zoom link and the runbook.

Action items:
1) Alice: upload the manifest + eval set (CSV) to the Drive folder and flag any datasets with additional redaction needs.
2) Marissa: will lead prompt review and evaluation criteria.
3) Karthik: I'll hand off routing/load test config to you for the session.

Thanks — I'll send the invite once Alice confirms the 9/14 slot.

—Jonas

Looping in the prompt/evals lead — quick notes to make the session productive:

Prompt review expectations:
- Please provide the eval CSV with columns: id, prompt_text, expected_response, tolerance (optional). The attached prompt_evals_template.csv is the schema we use.
- If you have disambiguation examples or multi-turn prompts, include a short context field.

Evaluation metrics we'll run during the hands-on:
- Exact-match / semantic-match, response length distribution, latency percentiles, and token cost per request.

Data hygiene / redaction:
- We can do automated masking for emails and phone numbers during ingest, but for laws-protected PII (national IDs) please remove before uploading. Redaction guide attached.

Logistics:
- I suggest we reserve the first 30 minutes for prompt review and redaction checks, then a 60-minute hands-on where we run the 5 RPS load window for 10 minutes in the middle, and finish with 20 minutes of result review.
- Timezone check: 9/14 10:00-12:00 PDT = 13:00-15:00 EDT; if you need an earlier slot we can also do 9/15 08:00-10:00 PDT.

I'll attach a small sample manifest (acme_sample_manifest.csv) — replace placeholder IDs with your real ones.

—Marissa
